audit.whatIsWrong: The remaining wrong-name references are in wants.you[0] and wants.foe[2], which still say 'his Q3 (the dash-knockup)' and 'Q double-tap' rather than Mortal Steel, and the full-layer tldr still lists 'Yone E return, third Q swing (the knock-up), R, and item spikes' — a template string that describes AATROX's third swing inside a list of Yone's threats.
audit.why: Riot's text: Mortal Steel — 'On hit, grants a stack of Gathering Storm for a few seconds. At 2 stacks, Mortal Steel dashes Yone forward with a gust of wind knocking enemies Airborne.' The knockup is gated on landing a first hit and holding the stack, so the punish window is the moment after his first Mortal Steel connects, not a flat cooldown. Soul Unbound leaves his body at a fixed point and forces his spirit back to it, which the mid text now states correctly.
audit.corrected: Mortal Steel named with its two-stack condition in wants.you[0]; Fate Sealed named in wants.foe[2]; the full tldr rewritten around Soul Unbound and Spirit Cleave.

edits.before: Yone changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Yone E return, third Q swing (the knock-up), R, and item spikes. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Yone wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Yone changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Soul Unbound (E, 22s), which leaves his body behind and snaps his spirit back to it, and Spirit Cleave (14s), which shields him by the number of champions it catches. Aatrox wins by standing on that body instead of chasing the spirit, spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, and fighting him alone in the side lane, where Spirit Cleave shields for the least it ever will.
